findings.title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` (which is now the default when a user has no destination calendar), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined`. Line 119 then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (`?.`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event with `MeetLocationType` (Google Meet) is created for a user without a destination calendar.

findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check breaks organization slug assignment
findings.body: Line 151 changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` in an unrelated file. Previously, `slug` was set directly only when billing was disabled, and stored as `metadata.requestedSlug` when billing was enabled until payment completed. With the inverted condition, self-hosted/non-billing instances (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED === false`) create organizations with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, while billing-enabled instances immediately assign `slug` before payment.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first host's destinationCalendar instead of matching the credential
findings.body: In a collective booking, `event.destinationCalendar` contains the destination calendars of all hosts, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent` once per host credential with the full `event`. Unlike `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` (which looks up the entry matching `credentialId`), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128 and 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) all take `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. When a secondary host uses Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV/Apple Calendar, their service will use the first host's `externalId` (e.g., a Google Calendar address), causing Office 365 and Lark API calls to fail with 404/invalid calendar ID and causing `BaseCalendarService` to filter out all calendars and silently skip creating the event.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent can never match and leaves calendarId undefined
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`undefined`, `null`, or `""`). Comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` against a falsy value will never match any `DestinationCalendar` (whose `externalId` is a non-empty string), so the fallback always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` also has no `"primary"` fallback, so `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`. Similarly, in `createEvent` (line 168), `calendar.events.patch` passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without `|| "primary"`, which is `undefined` when no `destinationCalendar` matches `credentialId`.

findings.title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer and eventType have no destinationCalendar
findings.body: Lines 1063-1067 initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `null` when both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are null. Line 1078 then executes `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. As a result, if the primary organizer has no `destinationCalendar` set, all other collective hosts' `destinationCalendar` entries in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent even when the referenced credential is undefined
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-543), if `reference.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup (`credentialFromDB`) returns `null` or has no `app.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` without checking `if (credential)`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` then accesses `credential.appName` (line 314) and throws a `TypeError`, causing `Promise.all(result)` to reject and abort updates for the remaining calendar references.

findings.title: updateLocation sets undefined externalCalendarId and credentialId on calendar references
findings.body: In `EventManager.updateLocation` (lines 201-211), `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. However, `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (called by `updateAllCalendarEvents`) does not populate `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` (nor does it set `createdEvent`), so calendar results in `updateLocation` produce duplicate `BookingReference` entries with `uid: ""`, `externalCalendarId: undefined`, and `credentialId: undefined`.
